Advantages:
C H A P I T R E 1
Solo Travel
A solo traveler explores the world on his own terms.	–
He experiences a sense of adventure that is exhilarating (=exciting and thrilling).	–
He enjoys a sense of freedom. In fact, he can choose where to go, what to eat and
when to rest as (=because) there are no rigid group schedules to follow or stick to. He
will just follow his curiosity that may lead him to an unexpected escapade (=thrilling
outdoor adventure).
–
He doesn't need to stick to a fixed itinerary and waste much time visiting crowded
attractions where even taking photos is a challenge or which are not his cup of tea.
–
Solo travel doesn't only allow the traveler to visit places off the beaten track (=not
commonly visited) that he may miss in a group, but it also allows him to explore any
place at his own pace.
–
Solo travel connects the traveler with others. For instance, he may have conversations
with the locals, who may share their stories or who may invite him to join them for a
meal or a tour. All these opportunities enrich his journey and create the most
memorable experiences as well.
–
It also allows him to have a journey of self-discovery; thus, he learns to trust his
instinct, to use technology while on the go, to embrace (=accept) the world around
him, to be tolerant, to step out of his comfort zone and to embark on (=start=begin) a
solo adventure of a lifetime that is truly unforgettable and life-changing.
–

ةﻮﻄﺨﺑ ةﻮﻄﺧ ..ﻚﺘﯾاﺮﻗ ﻲﻓ
Drawbacks:
→ He returns home disappointed because he spent all his savings to experience a
lifetime adventure, but he actually didn't enjoy his holiday to the fullest.
→ Facing the unexpected is not exciting, but it is rather stressful and frustrating.
→ The lesson a solo traveler may learn is the importance of companionship. After all,
the most memorable experiences are often better, richer, more exciting and safer
when shared.
Solo travel is stressful because the solo traveler has to prepare everything on his own,
and he spends too much time preparing a bucket list beforehand (=earlier).
–
He may face many unexpected challenges or problems that he can't solve by himself.
The most common one is the language when asking for directions or seeking
recommendations or information, or even when just trying to socialize with the locals.
Another major problem he may face is when some of his belongings (=possessions)
or official documents get lost or stolen and he can't get them back.
–
Despite the well-planned trip, the solo traveler may get lost and may be confused and
unable to take the right means of transport to get back to the hotel.
–
Another problem a solo traveler may face is solitude and loneliness. He feels lonely
and isolated, especially during meals, during which he is obliged to spend time sitting
quietly and scrolling through his mobile phone, just to distract himself from the
emptiness of the experience. Also, there will be no companion with whom he shares
the stress and feelings of frustration.
–
As a solo traveler who planned his own itinerary, he may make wrong decisions or
choices that may turn the trip into an unsafe or even a hellish experience.
–
A solo trip may be more expensive than a package holiday.	–
A solo traveler misses the discounts and the free services offered to package
holidaymakers by their tour operators.
–
